name: Pseudoephedrine

tolerance.full: develops with repeated and frequent use

addictionPotential: moderate addictive potential; can cause psychological dependence
toxicities: LD50 in rats is 1,674 mg/kg orally. Overdose may cause severe hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, stroke, and seizures.
summary: Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic drug of the phenethylamine and amphetamine chemical classes. It is used medically as a nasal/sinus decongestant and recreationally as a mild stimulant. It is structurally related to methamphetamine and is regulated as a precursor chemical in many countries.
effectsSummary: Mild to moderate stimulation, bronchodilation, appetite suppression, increased endurance, mild euphoria, vasoconstriction, increased heart rate and blood pressure, focus enhancement, anxiety at higher doses.
dosageRemark: Therapeutic decongestant doses are 30-60mg. Stimulant effects become noticeable at 60-120mg. Higher doses increase side effects disproportionately.
generalRisks: Increased heart rate and blood pressure, vasoconstriction, dry mouth, nausea, pupil dilation at high doses. Can cause anxiety and jitteriness.
longtermRisks: Moderate addiction potential with psychological dependence. Tolerance develops quickly. May cause cardiovascular strain with chronic use.
saferUse: Avoid if you have hypertension or heart conditions
